sehemu: Part II: Members of Parliament, Constituencies and Election of Members
maudhui: (1) There shall be an Electoral Commission of the United Republic whose members shall be appointed by the President and shall comprise: (a) a Chairman who is a Judge of the High Court or Court of Appeal, or a person qualified to be an advocate and who has held such qualification for not less than fifteen years; (b) a Vice-Chairman with the same judicial or professional qualifications; and (c) such other members as may be prescribed by a law enacted by Parliament. (2) The President shall appoint the Vice-Chairman in accordance with the principle that where the Chairman comes from one part of the Union, the Vice-Chairman shall come from the other part of the Union. (3) The following persons shall not be eligible for appointment as members of the Electoral Commission: (a) a Minister or Deputy Minister; (b) a person holding any office declared by law to be incompatible with membership; (c) a Member of Parliament, councillor or other person holding an office prescribed by law; or (d) a leader of any political party. (4) Subject to the other provisions of this Article, a member of the Electoral Commission shall cease to be a member: (a) upon expiry of five years from the date of appointment; or (b) if any circumstance arises which, if he were not a member, would render him ineligible for appointment. (5) The President may remove a member of the Electoral Commission from office only for inability to perform his functions, whether arising from illness or any other cause, misconduct, or loss of qualification for membership. (6) The functions of the Electoral Commission shall be: (a) to supervise and coordinate the registration of voters in presidential and parliamentary elections in the United Republic; (b) to supervise and coordinate the conduct of presidential and parliamentary elections; (c) to review constituency boundaries and divide the United Republic into areas for the election of Members of Parliament; (d) to supervise and coordinate the registration of voters and the conduct of elections of councillors; and (e) to perform any other functions in accordance with a law enacted by Parliament. (7) For the effective discharge of its functions, the Electoral Commission shall be an independent autonomous department, shall make its formal decisions concerning the discharge of its functions at meetings, and its chief executive shall be the Director of Elections. (8) Parliament may enact a law making provision for the procedure for supervising elections of Members representing constituencies. (9) The Electoral Commission may perform its functions notwithstanding a vacancy among its members, but every decision of the Commission shall be supported by a majority of its members. (10) Parliament may enact a law making provision for the procedure for appointing officers to supervise elections. (11) In exercising its powers under this Constitution, the Electoral Commission shall not be obliged to comply with orders or directions of any person, Government department or political party. (12) No court shall have jurisdiction to inquire into anything done by the Electoral Commission in the exercise of its powers. (13) In exercising its powers under this Constitution, the Electoral Commission of the United Republic shall from time to time consult the Electoral Commission of Tanzania Zanzibar. (14) Persons concerned with elections shall be prohibited from joining any political party, except that each shall have the right to vote. (15) For purposes of subarticle (14), persons concerned with elections are: (a) the Chairman of the Electoral Commission; (b) the Vice-Chairman; (c) all members of the Commission; (d) the Director of Elections and all employees of the Commission; and (e) all election supervisors in all cities and districts.
